turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `composition` (absorber), `architecture` (n-i-p =
regular, p-i-n = inverted), `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode),
`etl` (electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Each row is a device
CONFIGURATION whose efficiency is the median over at least 2 independently
fabricated cells, so it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single
champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_retention_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured
    percentage of the initial efficiency still retained at the end of a
    300–1200 h stability test (%).
  - b3_pvk_retention_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose percentage
    of the initial efficiency still retained at the end of a 300–1200 h
    stability test (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and the same
    device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST percentage
of the initial efficiency still retained at the end of a 300–1200 h
stability test (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
# Reasoning from Device Physics

## Key patterns in the training data (high-retention devices)

Looking at the configurations with retention ≥ 90%, several strong physical signatures emerge:

**1. Carbon back-contact + mesoporous TiO2/ZrO2 stacks (HTL-free)**
The very top of the training set is dominated by carbon-electrode, HTL-free mesoscopic architectures (`TiO2-c | TiO2-mp | ZrO2-mp | none | Carbon` → 97–100%; `CsPbBr | Carbon` → 95–98%). Carbon is inert (no metal migration, no electrode corrosion), and the absence of a small-molecule/hygroscopic HTL removes the biggest degradation pathway. These are the archetype of stable PSCs.

**2. All-inorganic / Cs-rich wide-gap compositions**
CsPbBr and CsPbBrI compositions cluster at very high retention (86–99%) because they lack the volatile MA/FA organic cation and resist thermal/moisture decomposition.

**3. Gold + Cs-containing triple-cation with robust dopant-free HTLs (PTAA)**
CsPbBrI/CsPbI with PTAA + Au reach 98–100% (no Li-TFSI hygroscopic doping, noble metal contact).

## Screening the candidate pool

I look for candidates matching the highest-retention motifs: **carbon electrodes + HTL-free mesoscopic stacks**, **all-inorganic Cs compositions**, and **dopant-free PTAA + noble metal on Cs-rich absorbers**.

Top matches:

- **c074**: `CsPbBr, TiO2-c | TiO2-mp | Graphene-QDs, none (HTL-free), Carbon` — matches the single most stable class (all-inorganic CsPbBr, mesoporous carbon, HTL-free, QD-passivated). Training analogs = 95–98%.
- **c027**: `MAPbI, TiO2-c | TiO2-mp, none, Carbon` — HTL-free mesoscopic carbon; training twin at 97% (`...TiO2-mp | ZrO2-mp | none | Carbon`) and 82.7%. Carbon + HTL-free is very robust.
- **c062**: `CsPbBrI, TiO2-c, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au` — all-inorganic wide-gap; CsPbBrI/Au configs sit at 87–93%.
- **c080**: `MAPbI, TiO2-c | TiO2-mp, none, Carbon` — same HTL-free carbon mesoscopic family as c027 (training analogs 76–97%).
- **c093**: `MAPbI, TiO2-c | TiO2-mp, TPDI, Carbon` — carbon electrode with a robust perylene-diimide-type HTL; carbon contact drives stability.

I favor c074 highest (all-inorganic + carbon + HTL-free = the two strongest stabilizing factors combined). Carbon/HTL-free MAPbI mesoscopic devices (c027, c080) are consistently high because the carbon eliminates electrode-driven and HTL-driven degradation even with the MA cation. c062 leverages inorganic composition + noble metal.

## Final Answer

**Final: c074, c027, c062, c080, c093**
